title: Documenting Temporal Coupling Requirements
pattern: Warning comments asserting strict temporal execution ordering requirements between independent public API methods.
why_bad: Runtime vulnerability. Nothing structurally prevents a developer from calling `configure()` first, resulting in silent memory bugs or invalid states. Temporal coupling should be enforced by the API structure.
detection: Comments containing 'must be called before' or 'call X first' on public struct methods.
counterexample: A typestate API (`fn initialize(self) -> ConfiguredDevice`) that makes out-of-order calls unrepresentable, needing no warning.
fix: Use the typestate pattern, forcing the transition structurally so that non-initialized configurations cannot compile.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 5.3 ("Temporal decomposition"); Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages* (2002).
